purpose: Machine-readable repository architecture contract for top-level ownership and lifecycle boundaries.

.github.note: GitHub-native automation boundary; remains at repository root by platform contract.

apps.note: Canonical container for maintained application source whose deployed URL layout is staged independently; contains the current Browser Rulebook, Card Reference, Deckbuilder, Factions, Rules, Start, Playtest, About, Accessibility, Changelog, Contact, FAQ, Press, and Privacy surfaces.

card-design.note: Rendering/authoring system; target split between shared rendering package and production tools.

config.note: Maintained cross-system configuration; root placement is deliberate.

docs.note: Maintained documentation and explicitly archived development records.

governance.note: Decision provenance, schemas, traceability, and audit records.

images.note: Source and derived visual assets remain mixed pending asset-lifecycle audit.

media.note: Current reproducible media/composition configuration and export tooling.

packages.note: Canonical container for maintained shared packages and authorities; contains the complete current game-data authority plus the maintained active rules source, publication support, and current rule-fact synchronization helper.

rulebook.note: Legacy monolithic Rulebook and version-specific compatibility support plus Rulebook QR assets. Gameplay authority lives at packages/game-data/current-game.json, active rules and maintained current rules support live at packages/rules/, and Browser Rulebook application source lives at apps/rulebook/.

rules-arbiter.note: Current static Rules Arbiter browser shell.

rules-assistant.note: Rules Arbiter implementation, retrieval, tests, and deployable endpoint.

scripts.note: Cross-project generation, validation, release, migration, and maintenance tooling.

tests.note: Repository-wide contract/regression harness; root placement is deliberate.

tts.note: TTS generation/packaging plus versioned release evidence.

v0.7.1.note: Lifecycle-selected current versioned public entrypoint; transitions to legacy when historical.
